title: Within-subject comparison of fixed and removable locator prostheses in the edentulous maxilla: A crossover randomized clinical trial
summary:
If, in patients with edentulous jaws, replacement of the teeth with a conventional mucosa-supported complete denture does not achieve sufficient oral health–related quality of life, the prosthesis can be stabilized by dental implants provided that suitable prerequisites are met. In the edentulous jaw, either fixed bridges are connected to the implants, or removable dentures are provided that are stabilized on the implants using prefabricated or individually fabricated retentive elements. In both cases, a demonstrable improvement in patients’ oral health–related quality of life is achieved compared with the baseline situation. In the edentulous maxilla, four implants should be placed for both restorative concepts in such a way that the prosthesis is supported over a wide span.
Patients and/or dentists may associate different expectations with the two treatment concepts regarding hygiene ability, complication rate, prognosis, effort, patient preference, satisfaction, and aesthetics. However, due to the available evidence and the lack of comparative studies, there is no differential risk assessment between the two prosthetic concepts. The effects of implant therapy and the restorative concept in the edentulous maxilla are still unclear from both a functional and a patient perspective. In some cases, anatomical or patient-specific prerequisites clearly favor one of the two options. In many cases, however, both variants are feasible, and the decision between fixed and removable restoration is largely guided by patient preference.

Because of the lack of direct comparisons, patients can scarcely assess whether they will be able to handle the retention elements of a denture, maintain adequate oral hygiene, or what impact the choice of prosthesis will have on phonetics and aesthetics. For dentists as well, the absence of data means that counseling edentulous patients on the choice of an implant-supported restoration remains one of the greatest challenges in implant planning. The study therefore aims to answer the following question: Do patients prefer fixed or removable implant-supported restorations in the edentulous maxilla when they have previously worn both variants with identical tooth arrangement, color, shape, and position, and identical abutments—and how do these two forms of prosthetic rehabilitation, and satisfaction with them, change over time?
conditions: Loss of teeth due to accident, extraction or local periodontal disease

interventions.name: Rehabilitation of the edentulous maxilla with four implants and implant-supported prostheses in two variants. Sequence (Arm 1): fixed restoration → after 3 months switch to removable → after a further 3 months final decision.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Willingness to participate
Ability to comply with the study protocol
Signed informed consent
Edentulous maxilla
Exclusion criteria:
Systemic/local contraindications to implant treatment
Medications that affect bone metabolism
Oromaxillofacial radiotherapy > 50 Gy (within the last 5 years)
Severe bruxism/teeth grinding
Smoking (> 10 cigarettes/day)
Pregnancy/breastfeeding
Non-compliance with treatment instructions; drug/alcohol abuse
Removable mandibular complete denture
